title: Ashbury Rewards Guidance on the Award-Activity Reduction
content:
Members who redeem Ashbury Rewards points often are recognised when a Reward Night Rate reservation is cancelled after the deadline or ends as a no-show: the retained share of the night value — the part of one night's points value that is not returned — is reduced by an award-activity reduction.

## Rule

The retained share is reduced by an award-activity reduction of fifteen percentage points when at least five award redemption transactions were posted on the account in the twelve months before the handling date, of five percentage points when two to four were posted, and of nothing when fewer were posted; the reservation's own redemption counts among them. The retained share after the reduction is never below zero percent.

The twelve months before the handling date are the transactions posted after the same day number twelve months earlier, up to and including the handling date. Only award redemption transactions are counted — not certificate top-offs and not redeposits.

| Award redemption transactions in the twelve months | Award-activity reduction |
|---|---|
| 5 or more | 15 percentage points |
| 2 to 4 | 5 percentage points |
| 0 or 1 | None |

## Cases (hypothetical accounts)

| Award redemptions in the window, the reservation's own included | Reduction |
|---|---|
| 1 (the reservation's own only) | None |
| 2 | 5 percentage points |
| 4 | 5 percentage points |
| 5 | 15 percentage points |

A retained share of 50 percent reduced by 15 percentage points is 35 percent; a retained share of 0 percent stays at 0 percent.
